A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same study. Their text, equations, six tables, seven figures, and Appendices A–E are readable and support reliable comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports original checkpoint analyses, full-versus-subnetwork fine-tuning experiments, subnetwork-overlap measurements, and training-dynamics analyses in Sections 3–6 and the appendices.

after.justification: v2 retains these original empirical results, including DPO/PRIME fine-tuning comparisons and the appendix checkpoint and tolerance analyses.

M1.justification: Both versions identify subnetworks from full fine-tuning's parameter differences and retrain using masked gradients. The procedure, training objectives, and model components are unchanged.

E1.justification: The same training data, checkpoint collections, and evaluation tasks are retained, including AGIEval, GPQA, MMLU Pro Math, MATH500, and AIME2024. The rejection-sampling and in-/out-of-distribution scenarios also remain unchanged.

E2.justification: The full-fine-tuning, SFT, random-overlap, and algorithm comparisons retain the same participants in corresponding experiments. ProRL is newly cited as a confounder in the limitations, but is not added as an evaluated comparator.

E3.justification: The evaluation procedures, bfloat16 precision, default 10^-5 sparsity tolerance, and Appendix B training settings are unchanged. The new numerical-precision discussion does not report a changed experimental setting.

E4.justification: Layerwise/rank analyses, overlap tests, KL/clipping comparisons, training-duration analyses, and distribution comparisons are retained. Appendix A's tolerance analysis and Appendix D's checkpoint trajectories are unchanged; the new precision explanation adds no experiment.

E5.justification: Seed information and statistical reporting practices are unchanged, with no added error bars, confidence intervals, or significance tests. The new checklist explicitly acknowledges the absence of significance reporting rather than introducing uncertainty estimation.

E6.justification: Tables 1–6 and Figures 1–7 retain their empirical values and findings. For example, both versions' Table 3 reports full/subnetwork DPO averages of 40.3/41.9 and PRIME overall accuracies of 69.8/72.2. The AGIEval spelling correction does not change a result.

T1.justification: The sparsity and overlap definitions, gradient-mask formulation, Conjecture 1, and Appendix E random-overlap calculation are unchanged. The added finite-precision footnote is an informal mechanism explanation, not a new mathematical derivation or proof.

C1.justification: v2 conditions the introduction's optimization claim on policy-aligned training and changes concentration 'entirely' within a subnetwork to 'primarily.' It also removes 'intrinsic' wording from the abstract and conclusion while retaining the principal empirical contributions.

C2.justification: Section 6 adds a conjecture that unlimited-precision updates would be dense, whereas finite precision discards tiny updates. Takeaway 4 recasts in-distribution training's causal role as conjectural, and Section 7 acknowledges ProRL as an unresolved confounder. These qualify the existing interpretation without replacing its main explanation.

D1.justification: v2 adds an authors' code-repository pointer in the abstract and identifies the Delta computing resource in the acknowledgments. The checklist newly describes most accuracy evaluations as deterministic. Appendix B hyperparameters and Appendix C checkpoint details remain unchanged.

R1.justification: v2 adds Liu et al. (2025a), ProRL: Prolonged Reinforcement Learning Expands Reasoning Boundaries in Large Language Models, and cites it in the limitations. The related-work discussion and positioning relative to lottery tickets, sparse training, and LoRA are otherwise unchanged.

P1.justification: v2 makes localized prose revisions and typo corrections, updates author/venue text, and adds acknowledgments and a NeurIPS checklist. The scientific sections retain their order and most of their wording; the appendices are textually unchanged apart from formatting.

P2.justification: All existing figures and table structures are retained. Figure 1 is slightly enlarged, existing figures and surrounding text are repositioned, and the added material changes pagination. Table 3 corrects the AGIEval label without changing numerical cells.

improvement.justification: The new code-access information and more conditional interpretation modestly improve transparency and calibration of the unchanged empirical evidence. The gain is limited: the finite-precision explanation receives no new validation, and the added checklist retains blank or TODO justifications.
